messages:
maya: FYI nightly perf job flagged a 28% tail-latency spike on kv-cache heavy traces this morning. attaching quick nsys summary.
oli: ugh. which model/seq len? any kernel fallbacks showing up?
maya: model=redwood-gpt-13b, seq=2048, batching heuristic changed last week (auto-batch tuning). nsys shows a ton of small kernels and repeated cudaMemcpys around kv-cache restore. kernel selection log: fallback to generic_matmul on a few shards.
cheng: small kernels + many launches == launch overhead. did the kernel selector prefer int8 kernels recently? those sometimes have narrower tiling and more launches.
maya: looks like quantization profile was toggled to q4_1 for that model by Optimize suggestions. selector preferred q4 matmul path, but when seq>1024 it falls back to generic path for some layers. fallback cost is high.
ram: can you paste the nsys capture cmd you used? want to replicate locally.
maya: sure:

```
nsys profile --sample=cpu --trace=cuda,cudnn --capture-range=exec --output=/tmp/trace_1998765432 
-- python -u run_inference.py --model redwood-gpt-13b --seq 2048 --batch 8
```

maya: then `tar -I pigz -cf trace_1998765432.tar.gz /tmp/trace_1998765432*` and upload to s3.
jess: how big were the traces? yesterday's were 4.2GB which is getting heavy for nightly retention.
maya: this one was 5.1GB raw, 900MB compressed with pigz. upload path: s3://redwood-ci-perf/traces/1998765432/redwood-gpt-13b/seq2048/
perf-bot: Perf baseline comparison complete. Regression: +28% 99p latency vs baseline build 1998600000. See diff dashboard: https://perf.redwood.ai/diff/1998600000...1998765432 :eyes:
oli: perf-bot link shows kernel timeline: many 10-40us kernels in tight loop. That smells like kernel selection chop.
cheng: possible approaches:
• adjust selector heuristics to favor few larger kernels for seq>1024
• add a cheap pre-check: if kv-cache restored size > X then force fused-matmul path
• batch coalescing to reduce launches

ram: for automation: can we have CI only persist traces when perf-bot detects >10% regression? otherwise discard to save S3.
jess: +1. also lifecycle rules: move to Glacier after 7 days, delete after 30 unless flagged by perf team.
maya: agreed. proposal for CI changes:
1) Run lightweight nsight sampling on every PR (nsys --sample=cpu) and upload metadata (tiny json) always.
2) Nightly full capture (nsys full trace) only when nightly-perf flag OR perf-bot regression >10% compared to baseline.
3) Compress with pigz and prune raw traces before upload.
4) Add a quick post-process script that extracts kernel timeline + top-10 kernels into a compact json for diff dashboard.

oli: The post-process json is key. current diff dashboard parses nsys CSV which is huge. compact json with aggregate kernel-name, count, total_time, avg_time should be enough.
cheng: I can prototype the post-process. plan: run `nsys stats --report=summary` then jq the CSV -> json line items and compute aggregates.

```
# pseudo
nsys stats -r trace_1998765432.qdrep -o summary
python tools/nsys_to_compact.py summary.csv > compact_1998765432.json
```

maya: CI implementation details: use existing runner `perf-smoke-runner` image, add env var `PERF_UPLOAD_THRESHOLD=0.10`.
ci-bot: New job created: perf/nightly-smoke-trace-runner (cron 02:30 UTC). Artifact step integrated with s3-uploader-v2.
jess: also add a presubmit check: if a PR changes kernel selector config files in `runtime/selector/heuristics` then schedule a gated nightly capture regardless of perf-bot result.
ram: good idea. selectors are sensitive.
oli: question: how to detect kv-cache restore pathological pattern automatically? maybe look for repeated `memcpyHtoD` spikes in compact json and flag.
cheng: yeah add rule: if top kernel is `memcpyHtoD` and it accounts for >20% of total GPU time and count > 200 -> mark trace as kv-hotspot.
maya: ok next steps: cheng to prototype `nsys_to_compact.py` and probe-rule; ram to update CI job + upload logic; jess to update S3 lifecycle and dashboard ingestion; oli will draft selector heuristic change RFC with simple fallback thresholds.
jess: timeline?
maya: aim for prototype in 1 week, full rollout in 3 weeks (so we can watch two nightly cycles).
oli: ping me if you need a perf baseline update. I can rebaseline builds.
perf-bot: noted. Will annotate diffs and attach compact json when available.
jess: thanks all :thumbsup:
maya: leaving the raw trace link here for now: s3://redwood-ci-perf/traces/1998765432/raw/trace_1998765432.qdrep.tar.gz
ram: i'll pull and run local sampler to triage. thanks!
